OpenClaw 🦞 — Your assistant, on your devices, in your chats OpenClaw is an open-source AI assistant that runs on your own computer and meets you in the channels you already use: Discord, iMessage, Slack, Teams, Telegram, WhatsApp, and 20+ more, plus native apps for macOS, iOS, Android, Windows, and Linux. One Gateway runs it as a personal assistant on a laptop or as a shared team deployment ; configuration is the only difference. Yours, with no catch. State, memory, and credentials live on your hardware. Models and agent harnesses (Claude, Codex, local models) are plugins you can swap without changing anything else. Your prompts go to the model provider and chat platforms you configure, plus any diagnostics export you enable yourself; by default OpenClaw itself phones home for nothing but a daily version check, anonymous feature statistics are opt-in, and update.checkOnStart: false disables both ( what OpenClaw sends ). OpenClaw is stewarded by the OpenClaw Foundation , an independent 501(c)(3), and has no paid tier, hosted service, or token. The architecture case — trusted gateway, untrusted execution, policy enforced by code — is in Why OpenClaw . Website · Docs · Getting started · Why OpenClaw · FAQ · Vision · DeepWiki Install The installer supports macOS, Linux, and Windows. It provisions a supported Node.js runtime when needed. # macOS / Linux / WSL2 curl -fsSL https://openclaw.ai/install.sh | bash # Windows PowerShell iwr - useb https: // openclaw.ai / install.ps1 | iex Already manage Node.js? Install the published package instead (Node 24.16+ or 26.1+; Node 26 recommended): npm install -g openclaw@latest --allow-scripts=openclaw That command is for npm 12 or npm 11.16+. On npm 11.15 and earlier, omit --allow-scripts=openclaw . See the installation guide for the lifecycle script
contract, Docker, Nix, and other deployment paths. Quick start On a fresh install, the installer scripts start onboarding automatically.
Complete the wizard they open. If you installed the package directly with npm,
pnpm, or Bun, run: openclaw onboard --install-daemon After onboarding: openclaw gateway status
openclaw dashboard Onboarding verifies model access, creates the workspace, and configures the Gateway. The last command opens the Control UI; send a message there to confirm the assistant is working. See the getting started guide for channel setup and troubleshooting. How it fits together The Gateway is the local control plane for sessions, tools, events, and channel connections. The Control UI , CLI, and TUI connect to the Gateway. Channels bring the assistant to WhatsApp, Telegram, Slack, Discord, Google Chat, Signal, iMessage, and other messaging services. Companion apps and nodes add voice, Canvas, camera, screen, and device-local actions on supported platforms. OpenClaw works with hosted and local model providers . Its tools , skills , and plugins extend what an assistant can do. Security Treat inbound messages as untrusted input. DM-capable channels pair unknown senders by default; approve a pairing request with openclaw pairing approve <channel> <code> . Tools run on the host for the main session unless you configure sandboxing. Read the security guide , exposure runbook , and sandboxing guide before connecting other users or exposing the Gateway remotely. Documentation Goal Start here Configure models and auth Models · Model providers Connect a messaging service Channels Add tools, skills, and plugins Tools · Skills · Plugins · ClawHub Run apps and device nodes Platforms · Nodes Use the CLI and chat commands CLI reference · Slash commands Configure or operate the Gateway Configuration · Architecture · Updating · Release channels Development The repository is a pnpm workspace. Plain npm install at the repository root is not supported. git clone https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw.git cd openclaw
pnpm install
pnpm build
pnpm ui:build See CONTRIBUTING.md for the contribution workflow and the source setup guide for the development loop. Governance OpenClaw is developed in the open by the OpenClaw Foundation , an independent 501(c)(3). The Foundation employs the core team and signs releases. Donors and infrastructure sponsors support the Foundation; none of them own or direct the project. OpenAI is a donor, not an owner. Community See CONTRIBUTING.md for maintainers and contribution guidelines; AI-assisted PRs are welcome. Use the issue chooser for bugs and feature requests, ask setup questions in Discord , and report vulnerabilities through SECURITY.md . New capabilities usually belong in plugins built on the plugin SDK and shared through ClawHub . OpenClaw was built for Molty , a space lobster AI assistant, by Peter Steinberger and the community. Explore the project lore , soul.md , Peter's site , Star History , and @openclaw . Special thanks to Mario Zechner for his support and for pi , and to Adam Doppelt for the lobster.bot domain. Donors and sponsors The Foundation is funded by donors including Amazon, Lobster Computer Company, Offline Holdings, OpenAI, Red Hat, and the University of Michigan, with infrastructure support from Blacksmith, Convex, GitHub, NVIDIA, and Vercel. Contributors Thanks to all clawtributors: License MIT © OpenClaw Foundation. See THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md for incorporated or adapted code.

github.abstract:
dsh-pet 🐾 一隻住在 DeepSeek Harness 裡的桌面寵物：待機呼吸、隨機動作（打瞌睡、玩魔方、吃火鍋……）、左右轉向、螢幕漫遊、點選 Q 彈、拖拽甩拋反彈、右鍵選單點播——一百餘個透明動畫隨時無縫銜接；還能跟隨 DSH 會話事件切換工作狀態動畫、按檔位播放餘額動畫 + 頭頂氣泡、碎碎念與對話聊天、視窗失焦時彈系統通知。可多開同屏，能脫離瀏覽器住上 桌面 （透明置頂小窗），也能自己新增 全新寵物種類 （pet pack）。 這不是一個普通外掛，而是 完整的三件套專案 ： ① 提示詞（配方）    →  ② 素材生成鏈（引擎）  →  ③ 外掛（成品）
AI 生成動畫的配方     源影片 → 透明動畫的管線    執行在 DSH 裡的寵物 任何人 clone 本倉庫，都可以 從零生成自己的桌面寵物 ——換角色、換動作、換風格，全流程可復現。 快速開始（安裝外掛） 裝法取決於你在用哪個 DSH： 🪟 桌面應用（Electron 版） 直接在應用內「外掛管理」頁的安裝框裡填 dsh-pet ，不用開終端；需要在終端裡操作外掛時，用桌面應用自帶的那份 CLI。 🌐 dsh web 以下命令都在你的 命令列終端 （PowerShell / CMD 等）中執行。前提是 DSH 環境已就緒： # ① 前置要求：確認 Node.js 已安裝 node -v # ② 安裝 DSH 啟動器與 pnpm（已裝可跳過；裝完請重新開啟終端） npm install -g @deepseek-ai/dsh pnpm
dsh --version # 驗證 dsh 命令可用 # ③ 安裝本外掛（web 模式用 --profile web） dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-pet 裝完 重開桌面應用 （ dsh web 使用者則重啟 dsh web ）才生效——執行中的程序持有記憶體裡的舊外掛。寵物出現在介面右上角（預設配置角落，可在設定頁修改）。 相容性 ：本外掛當前在 dsh 0.2.1-rc.2 下開發並測試（ dsh --version 可檢視你的版本）。建議使用相同版本；其他版本如遇問題歡迎反饋。 從原始碼安裝（clone 本倉庫後） lib/ 構建產物不入庫，clone 後需要先構建再安裝： # ① clone 本倉庫，進入外掛目錄 git clone https://github.com/PC2005-cloud/dsh-pet.git cd dsh-pet/dsh-pet # ② 安裝依賴 npm install # ③ 構建（完整 lib：tsdown → lib + 桌面共享核心 + 型別宣告） npm run build # 必須手動跑一次（克隆後 npm install 不再自動構建） # ④ 安裝到 DSH（file: 指向**外掛目錄**——上面 cd 進去的那一層，用構建好的 lib） # --profile 填實際在用的那個：dsh web → web； # 桌面應用（Electron 版）改用應用內「外掛管理」安裝，見上方快速開始 dsh plugin --profile web add file:D:/path/to/dsh-pet/dsh-pet 注： npm run build （即 scripts/prepare.js ）才產出 完整可安裝 的 lib——除 tsdown 構建外還構建桌面共享核心（ shared-core.js ）、生成型別宣告並收斂釋出 files 清單；裸 tsdown 構建會缺桌面執行時與型別。釋出與打包（ npm publish / npm pack ）時由 prepack 自動呼叫它，克隆倉庫後需手動跑一次。 安裝後你會看到什麼 預設配置是 display: "both" （瀏覽器與桌面都顯示），所以重開 DSH 之後會依次出現兩處，不必手動開： 瀏覽器端先出現。 寵物落在介面右上角（預設角落，設定頁可改），此時桌面上還是空的。 宿主自動補桌面執行時。 本機沒有 Electron 時，外掛會自己下載一份（落在 ~/.dsh/electron ，同一版本只下一次；預設走 npmmirror 映象）。進度直接打在 DSH 的控制台裡，形如： [dsh-pet] Electron not found, downloading to <使用者目錄>/.dsh/electron/electron.exe ...
[dsh-pet] Electron not found, downloading v43.3.0 (win32-x64) ...
[dsh-pet] downloading 42.3MB / 104.1MB
[dsh-pet] download complete (37.5s), extracting to <使用者目錄>/.dsh/electron ... 這一步在 後臺 進行，瀏覽器裡的寵物照常可用；要等多久取決於網速（幾十秒到幾分鐘），期間不用管它。 桌面端隨後出現。 解壓完自動拉起桌面 Helper，同一只寵物以透明窗形式落到桌面上—— 此時螢幕上一共兩隻 ：瀏覽器裡一隻、桌面上那隻，共用同一份配置與同一套動畫。 想只留一隻。 兩條路都行，改完即時生效： 設定頁 ：選中該寵物 →「顯示位置」下拉框 → 僅瀏覽器 / 僅桌面 / 兩者都顯示 / 都不顯示； 寵物右鍵 ：選單裡的「顯示位置」子選單 → 僅網頁 / 僅桌面 / 兩者 / 都不（不用回設定頁）。 已經裝過 Electron（或設了 DSH_PET_ELECTRON_PATH 指向現成執行檔）時，第 2 步會跳過，桌面端幾乎立刻出現。下載失敗 隻影響桌面模式 ：控制台會給出提示，瀏覽器裡的寵物不受影響；網路受限時可以設 DSH_PET_ELECTRON_MIRROR 換映象、 DSH_PET_ELECTRON_VERSION 指定版本，重啟後再試。 💬 反饋與發版節奏 歡迎提 issue 與 PR——bug、體驗問題、最佳化想法都行。但動手前請先翻一眼 提交記錄 ，確認不是已經修掉的同款問題（有些問題可能已經在 main 上修好了，只是還沒發版）。 小修不單獨發版 ：不影響使用的小 bug 與最佳化會 累計 到下一個版本一起發，避免版本更迭過於頻繁。所以「 main 上已經修了」不等於「你裝的這版已經包含」—— latest 沒更新時，以 main 的提交記錄為準。 想立刻用上未釋出的修復 ：按上面的「從原始碼安裝」把外掛指向本地倉庫即可；注意 宿主半側 的程式碼改動要 重開 DSH 才生效（瀏覽器半側重新整理頁面即可）。 報 bug 時請帶上 ：外掛版本、 dsh 版本、作業系統、復現步驟（有日誌或截圖更好）。 外掛功能 純粹的桌寵 ：不做天氣、監控等無關功能，不碰 DSH 核心；可選能力只有下面這些（餘額 / 碎碎念 / 對話 / 工作狀態 / 系統通知） 動畫鏈 ：每個動畫（含待機）播完即按權重選下一個（預設 idle 10 / turn 5 / move 5 + 分類權重， config.jsonc 可調），首尾相接 事件動畫 ：餘額 / 碎碎念 / 工作狀態按檔位觸發專屬動畫；檔位支援候選陣列——觸發時檔內隨機、迴圈播放自動輪換，避免連播同一段 多開 ：同時顯示多個寵物，各自獨立大小與位置（設定頁「桌寵配置」新增/刪除） 螢幕漫遊 ：朝朝向方向行走，先探測空間、不走出螢幕（多屏按各屏邊界判定；設定頁「鎖定在當前螢幕」開啟後只在當前所在那塊屏內走） 點選 / 拖拽 / 甩拋 ：點選有回應動畫並 Q 彈擠壓；拖拽過阻尼彈簧跟手，甩出即拋物線飛行、螢幕邊緣反彈、落地摩擦停穩並 Q 彈一下；溫柔放下原地停住；兩端同一套純函式物理與擠壓曲線（ dsh-pet/src/shared/physics.ts ） 右鍵選單 ：「動作 → 分類 → 具體動畫」任意點播（移動類動畫點播會真實行走一段）；工具項——瀏覽器端：碎碎念 / 對話 / 回到初始位置；桌面端：+ 開啟網站、檢視餘額（餘額啟用時顯示）、過載配置（改完配置檔案直接右鍵過載全部桌面寵物，不必回設定頁點儲存） 「開啟網站」按宿主自動分派 ：寵物宿主是 DSH 桌面應用 時，該項自動變成「開啟 DeepSeek Harness」——用應用自注冊的 dsh://open 協議把桌面應用主視窗喚到前臺（已執行則前置、未執行則拉起）；宿主是 dsh web / 獨立模式時，仍是系統預設瀏覽器開啟站點 朝向與落地 ：全部動畫可映象（可朝左 / 朝右）；腳底線統一，寵物始終站在地面上 流暢切換 ：雙緩衝交叉淡入，切換無空白幀 餘額展示 ：按已用百分比分檔播餘額動畫 + 頭頂聯想氣泡（10 秒自動消失）；DeepSeek 顯示賬戶餘額，OpenCode Zen Go 與 Command Code 顯示最緊迫的一個額度視窗； 未登記餘額介面的服務商改為彈文字說明 （不靜默）；按寵物獨立開關 碎碎念與對話 ：碎碎念按週期自動生成一句（說話動畫 + 氣泡，也可手動觸發）；對話在右鍵彈輸入框與寵物聊天，記憶持久化（瀏覽器 / 桌面共享同一份） 工作狀態聯動 ：監聽 DSH 會話事件，切「思考 / 工作 / 整理 / 等待 / 成功 / 出錯」檔位動畫 + 常駐氣泡；目標多輪任務只在真正收尾輪慶祝 系統通知 ：視窗失焦時彈系統 toast（對話完成 / 生成失敗 / 輸出截斷 / 許可權申請 / 使用者選擇） 桌面模式（可選） ：每隻寵物開一個獨立透明置頂局部小窗，與瀏覽器嚴格同行為、共用同一份素材與純邏輯（見下節） pet pack（額外寵物種類） ： pet/ 下建 種類名-config.json + 種類名-animation/ 即新增獨立動畫池與素材的全新種類，多例項共享素材（見「配置 → 方式四」） 自定義動畫 ：往 main-animation/webm/ 放 VP9-Alpha 的 .webm 即為新動畫，優先於包內素材 無障礙 ：支援 prefers-reduced-motion （減少動效時跳過 Q 彈擠壓與淡入切換） 🔌 對外介面（供其他外掛呼叫） 桌寵不只自己玩，也 對外開放兩條呼叫通道 ，讓別的外掛或指令碼能驅動它、讀它的狀態。 能做什麼 ：讓它說一句指定的話、播一段指定動畫、與它對話；讀它當前說的話、工作狀態、系統通知與餘額 為什麼開放 ：桌寵不該只是個擺設——比如一個「女僕」外掛巡檢驗完想說句話，就能讓桌寵當它的「實體」開口；也方便任何人基於它做二次開發 通道一 · HTTP ：掛在 DSH 自己的 Web 服務上（字首 /dsh-pet-7340 npm run build && npm run standalone # 倉庫裡（先構建） 能用 ：動畫鏈、點選/拖拽/甩拋、右鍵選單、多開、自定義動畫與表情包、pet pack。 不可用 ：餘額、碎碎念、對話、系統通知——返回帶 reason 的結構化失敗（見 API.md ）。 配置 ：與 DSH 同一份（ $DSH_HOME/dsh-pet/main-config.jsonc → 包內預設）。 只顯示 display 含 desktop / both 的例項 ；埠預設 3080； Ctrl+C 或 POST /shutdown 退出。 與 DSH 內執行可同時開 ，但共用 %APPDATA%\dsh-pet-electron-helper ，可能互相踩快取（僅告警）。 ⚙️ 餘額展示（Balance） 按 eventsRefreshSec.balance （秒）週期拉取當前服務商的餘額/用量資料，每次重新整理按檔位觸發一次餘額動畫，並在寵物頭頂彈出 聯想氣泡 （隨寵物大小等比縮放，10 秒自動消失）： DeepSeek 官方（ deepseek-official ） ：氣泡顯示賬戶餘額（如 餘額 ¥8.79 ）；餘額按 ¥20 滿額折算成已用百分比，分 6 檔播放動畫（錢袋滿溢 → 金袋叮噹 → 錢袋如常 → 數金皺眉 → 袋空如洗 → 分文不剩） OpenCode Zen Go（ opencode-go ） ：氣泡顯示 5h/周/月 三個額度視窗中最先告急的一個（如 周額度已用 88% / 2.5 天重置 ），同樣按已用百分比分檔 Command Code（ commandcode ，含 GOAT 等套餐） ：氣泡顯示 5h/周/月 三個額度視窗中最先告急的一個（與 opencode 同一口徑：剩餘額度最少者，通常先報 5h）；套餐無視窗限制時只報月度窗 暫不支援的服務商 ：未登記餘額介面的服務商 不播檔位動畫，改為彈一句文字說明 ——第一行「當前服務商暫不支援餘額查詢」，第二行報出當前 provider id（便於自查）；缺憑證 / 抓取失敗同理（原因寫在第二行）。自動輪詢只在 原因變化 時彈一次（不反覆打擾），手動 /balance 或桌面右鍵「檢視餘額」則每次都會彈 按寵物開關 ： pets[i].balanceEnabled （必填布林）控制該寵物是否觸發餘額動畫/顯示氣泡 所需憑據 ：對應 provider 的 API key（ deepseek-official → DEEPSEEK_API_KEY ； opencode-go → OPENCODE_GO_API_KEY ； commandcode → COMMANDCODE_API_KEY ），在 DSH 憑據中配置後啟用；未匹配的服務商不觸發動畫，改為彈上面的文字說明氣泡 ⚙️ 碎碎念與對話 碎碎念 ： pets[i].whisperEnabled 開啟後，按 eventsRefreshSec.whisper （秒，預設 300）週期自動生成一句——每隻寵物獨立週期、獨立文案；觸發時隨機抽 events.whisper 動畫 + 頭頂說話氣泡（10 秒消失）。預設開啟 手動觸發 ：右鍵選單「碎碎念」隨時來一句——不受 whisperEnabled 門控（該欄位只關自動週期輪詢） 對話 ：右鍵選單「對話」或 /chat 命令開啟輸入框，與寵物聊天——回覆走碎碎念同款展示（說話動畫 + 氣泡）；記憶持久化在 $DSH_HOME/dsh-pet/memory.json ，瀏覽器與桌面共享同一份；多寵物時先用 /pet 選擇對話目標 ⚙️ 工作狀態聯動（Work Status） pets[i].

Claude SEO: SEO Skill for Claude Code Claude SEO is an open-source SEO analysis plugin for Claude Code . It runs 26 sub-skills and 19 specialist agents in parallel across technical SEO, content quality (E-E-A-T), Schema.org markup, AI search optimization (GEO), local SEO, e-commerce, and international SEO. Every audit produces a prioritized action plan with testable recommendations grounded in primary-source guidance from Google. Two versions of this skill. 🌐 Public open-source → AgriciDaniel/claude-seo : MIT, public releases, no membership. Use this if you want stable + downloadable. 🔒 Community private mirror → AI-Marketing-Hub/claude-seo : early access to upcoming features and direct collaboration with the AI Marketing Hub Pro community. Requires membership. Why Claude SEO AI-search first. Aligned with Google's AI Optimization Guide . Question-based citability scoring, primary-source evidence on llms.txt, IPTC TrainedAlgorithmicMedia for AI-generated product images, agent-friendly page checks per web.dev , and /seo agentic for agent readiness scored the way Lighthouse's Agentic Browsing category counts it. Parallel execution. Full site audits spawn up to 17 specialist agents simultaneously. Site-level audits complete in minutes rather than hours. Falsifiable, not promotional. Every recommendation carries the first-principle observation it rests on, its dependency relationships, an explicit "how would we know this failed?" check, and a leading indicator. See Methodology . Real results Who this is for SEO agencies running 5+ client sites. Replace quarterly deep audits with weekly automated runs. Same team capacity, 4× audit cadence, every recommendation comes with a falsifiability check the client can verify. In-house SEO leads at SaaS / publisher / e-commerce companies. Second-pair-of-eyes before executive reviews. Catches what GSC and Lighthouse hide: schema deprecation, AI-citability gaps, expired-domain heritage risk, parasite-SEO exposure, machine-translation drift. Freelance SEO consultants. Anchor day-one client scope with a 15-minute audit and a real 0-100 score. Win the engagement with concrete proof of value before you spend an hour writing the proposal. Run a full audit and watch parallel agents fan out across the site: Watch the full demo on YouTube Table of Contents Who this is for Installation Quick Start Commands Features Compared to manual / agency / commercial tools Use cases Sample Output Architecture Methodology What's New in v2 Limitations Requirements Uninstall Extensions Ecosystem Documentation FAQ License Contributing Author Installation ℹ️ Which version are you installing? Public open-source (default). The commands below install from AgriciDaniel/claude-seo : MIT, public releases, no membership required. AI Marketing Hub Pro member? Install the community version with early access instead: swap AgriciDaniel/claude-seo for AI-Marketing-Hub/claude-seo and the plugin slug claude-seo@agricidaniel-claude-seo for claude-seo@ai-marketing-hub-claude-seo . Plugin Install (Claude Code 1.0.33+) The fastest path. One-time marketplace add, then plugin install: /plugin marketplace add AgriciDaniel/claude-seo

images <url> Image optimization analysis /seo plan <type> Strategic SEO planning (saas, local, ecommerce, publisher, agency) /seo programmatic <url> Programmatic SEO analysis and planning /seo competitor-pages <url> Competitor comparison page generation /seo local <url> Local SEO analysis (GBP, citations, reviews, map pack) /seo maps [command] Maps intelligence (geo-grid, GBP audit, reviews, competitors) /seo hreflang <url> Hreflang / i18n SEO audit and generation /seo google [command] Google SEO APIs (GSC, PageSpeed, CrUX, Indexing, GA4, PDF reports) /seo backlinks <url> Backlink profile analysis (Moz, Bing, Common Crawl) /seo cluster <keyword> SERP-based semantic clustering /seo sxo <url> Search Experience Optimization (page-type, user stories, personas) /seo drift baseline | compare | history <url> SEO drift monitoring with SQLite snapshots /seo ecommerce <url> E-commerce SEO and marketplace intelligence /seo flow [stage] FLOW framework prompts (CC BY 4.0, evidence-led) /seo image-gen [use-case] AI image generation for SEO assets (extension) /seo seranking [command] AI Share-of-Voice across ChatGPT, Gemini, Perplexity, AI Overviews, AI Mode (extension) /seo profound [command] LLM citation tracking with time-series data (extension) /seo bing [command] <url> Bing Webmaster Tools + IndexNow URL submission (extension) /seo unlighthouse <url> Multi-page Lighthouse runner, runs locally (extension) Every extension command is documented in docs/COMMANDS.md . Features What Core Web Vitals does Claude SEO check? Claude SEO measures the current three Core Web Vitals: LCP (Largest Contentful Paint, target under 2.5s), INP (Interaction to Next Paint, target under 200ms), and CLS (Cumulative Layout Shift, target under 0.1). INP replaced FID on March 12, 2024; FID was removed from Chrome's field-data tools (CrUX API, PageSpeed Insights) on September 9, 2024 (Lighthouse is a lab tool and never reported FID), and Claude SEO never references FID. Field data comes from the Chrome User Experience Report (CrUX) when available; lab data falls back to Lighthouse via PageSpeed Insights.

github.title: ModernRelay/omnigraph

Object-storage native graph database with branching and typed ontology. Unified retrieval engine (vector/bm25/graph) · Git-style workflows · Open data format (Lance) Quickstart · Docs · Cookbooks · CLI llms.txt Omnigraph is engineered for the new workload introduced by long-horizon agents: Multiple agents sharing a typed world model to continuously retrieve and store context and coordinate work. Agents and UIs can become thin stateless consumers of a durable state. Capabilities Capability What it gives you Typed ontology Agents share one enforceable model of the domain. .pg schemas declare node and edge types, keys and constraints, and the engine enforces them on every write. Multimodal retrieval Agents assemble high-precision context in one query: graph traversal + vector ANN + full-text + Reciprocal Rank Fusion in one runtime, with filtering. Branching Agents propose reviewable changes instead of writing to main: a branch per agent or task, three-way merge, time travel across the whole graph. Declared as code A cluster.yaml declares graphs, schemas, stored queries, embedding providers and policies. cluster plan previews, cluster apply converges, Terraform-style. Security as code Cedar policy enforced server-side on every mutation , per graph or server-wide; bearer auth, server-resolved actors, audit tracking. Object-storage native, open format Scales at the lowest cost on local disk or any S3-compatible store: RustFS / MinIO, AWS S3 / R2 / GCS, Azure preview. Data lives in open, versioned Lance with native blob-as-data, and never leaves your store. What you can build Use case What it's for Company brain Org knowledge unified into one graph every agent can query Agentic memory Durable, versioned memory: a branch per agent or per task, merged on review Context graph Decision traces and codified tribal knowledge for retrieval Dev graph Issues & dependency model that coding agents read and write R&D / ML data layer Experiments and trials written into branches, versioned for training & eval Install curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ModernRelay/omnigraph/main/scripts/install.sh | bash This installs omnigraph (CLI) and omnigraph-server into ~/.local/bin from
published release binaries. Or with Homebrew: brew tap ModernRelay/tap
brew install ModernRelay/tap/omnigraph Set it up with an AI agent Omnigraph is built to be run by coding agents. Two ways in: Teach your agent the playbook. The omnigraph binary carries the omnigraph agent skill written for it: the operational
playbook covering cluster mode, the two config surfaces, schema evolution, query
linting, data writes, branches, Cedar policy, and the common gotchas. Export it
where your agent loads skills, so the skill always matches the installed CLI: omnigraph skill export ~ /.claude/skills/omnigraph --force With an older CLI that has no skill command, or none installed, npx skills add ModernRelay/omnigraph@omnigraph installs the copy on the
default branch instead. Or have an agent set it up from scratch. Paste this into Claude Code,
Codex, or any agent that can read a URL and run a shell command: Help me set up Omnigraph

1. Read the docs at https://github.com/ModernRelay/omnigraph, starting with
   docs/user/clusters/index.md, then docs/user/deployment.md.
2. Skim the starter graphs and seed data in the cookbooks:
   https://github.com/ModernRelay/omnigraph-cookbooks
3. Ask me what I want to build (company brain, agent memory, dev graph,
   research / R&D layer, …). Then stand up a cluster for it, load a little
   data, and run a query so I can see it working. For ready-to-run graphs with real seed data (company brain, VC operating system,
pharma & industry intel), ModernRelay/omnigraph-cookbooks is the fastest way to see Omnigraph shaped to a real domain. Deploy A deployment is a cluster : a multigraph config directory that declares
its graphs, schemas, stored queries, and policies as code. You manage it Terraform-style : cluster plan previews the diff, cluster apply converges
it. omnigraph-server then boots from the cluster and brings every graph online
at /graphs/{id}/… , each behind its own policy. 1. Declare the cluster. company-brain/
├── cluster.yaml
├── people.pg          # schema for the "knowledge" graph
├── queries/           # stored queries: the .gq files ARE the declaration
│   └── people.gq
└── base.policy.yaml   # a Cedar policy bundle # cluster.yaml version : 1 metadata : name : company-brain storage : s3://company/clusters/company-brain # ledger, catalog, and graph data live here graphs : knowledge : schema : people.pg queries : queries/ # every `query <name>` in queries/*.gq registers policies : base : file : base.policy.yaml applies_to : [knowledge] # graph-bound; use [cluster] for server-level 2. Stand up your object store. On-prem, run RustFS (or MinIO); Omnigraph
writes Lance over the standard S3 API.
In the cloud, use S3 / R2 / GCS through AWS_* . Native az:// roots are also
available as a qualification preview. Every Azure writer, including cluster apply and the server, must use the checked-in admission wrapper;
follow the Azure deployment guide instead of running the bare commands below. 3. Converge and run. apply creates each graph, applies its schema, and
publishes queries and policies into the content-addressed catalog. It is
idempotent; re-running is always safe. omnigraph cluster validate # parse + typecheck everything omnigraph cluster plan --target ./company-brain # preview omnigraph cluster apply --target ./company-brain # converge # Boot the server from the cluster dir; storage resolves through cluster.yaml omnigraph-server --cluster company-brain --bind 0.0.0.0:8080 The bare commands above describe local and S3 deployments. See the cluster guide for the day-2 loop
(edit → plan → apply → restart), approval gates for destructive changes, drift
inspection, and recovery; the deployment guide for
containers, AWS/Railway/Azure, auth, and the object-store environment contracts. Query and mutate Define a server target with default_graph and set defaults.target once in ~/.omnigraph/config.yaml ( configuration ), and the
everyday commands stay short. Stored queries and mutations run by name : omnigraph query  search_docs --params ' {"q":"AI safety"} ' omnigraph mutate add_person  --params ' {"name":"Mina"} ' # Branch, review, merge across the whole graph; agents write in isolation omnigraph branch create --from main agent/ingest-42
omnigraph branch merge  agent/ingest-42 --into main An alias is shorter still: bind a target, graph, and stored query to one
name, then omnigraph alias triage runs it. For an ad-hoc target, any command
takes --target NAME|ADDRESS , plus --graph ID for a graph within a server
or direct root. Use --target ./graph.omni for a standalone graph. See the CLI reference . Security & governance Engine-wide enforcement: every write path goes through the same Cedar gate, so the HTTP server, the CLI, and the embedded SDK obey identical rules. Declared in the cluster: a policy bundle is bound to graphs (or the whole server) via policies: → applies_to . Scoped: rules apply per graph, per branch, or server-wide. No plaintext tokens: bearer tokens are hashed at startup and compared in constant time. Forge-proof identity: the actor is resolved server-side from the token; clients can't set it. See the policy guide . Clients & SDKs Client Use it for Where TypeScript SDK typed access from Node / TS @modernrelay/omnigraph · source MCP server bridge Omnigraph to LLM hosts (Claude, Codex, …) @modernrelay/omnigraph-mcp HTTP / OpenAPI any language, the wire contract the server's OpenAPI spec Python SDK typed access from Python coming soon Both npm packages are versioned in lockstep with omnigraph-server .

github.abstract: MangoDisk Disk cleanup, storage analysis, and privacy protection for macOS , Windows , and Linux English · 簡體中文 · 繁體中文 · 日本語 · 한국어 · Русский What MangoDisk Can Do Storage 1. Deep Cleanup Find cleanable content scattered across the system, applications, developer tools, and local projects in one scan. MangoDisk saves you from checking each location manually and groups the results by reclaimable space: System and user caches : Reclaim space taken up over time by system temporary files, diagnostic data, and rebuildable caches. Application caches : Keep application caches, logs, update packages, and temporary content from quietly consuming more and more storage. Browser data : Reclaim space used by cached and temporary web data from Chrome, Edge, Firefox, Brave, Arc, Opera, and other browsers. Developer tools and Xcode : Quickly recover substantial storage used by package managers, IDEs, compiler caches, and Xcode development data. Container caches : Free up space used by inactive build caches and rebuildable data from Docker and other container tools. Project build artifacts : Recover space used by rebuildable dependencies, caches, and build directories across Node.js, Rust, Gradle, Swift, Python, .NET, Godot, CMake, and other projects. AI models and caches : Quickly spot large local AI models, download caches, and temporary transfer files. Application optimization : Shrink supported applications without affecting normal use, leaving more room on your disk. Smart recommendations help you make safe choices quickly. You can also review items individually and see the estimated reclaimable space upfront, keeping every cleanup predictable and under your control. 2. Large File Cleanup Quickly find the largest files and reclaim space used by old installers, videos, archives, and other bulky content without digging through folders one by one. 3. Duplicate File Cleanup Reclaim space taken up by duplicate copies without treating files as duplicates just because they share a name. Smart selection keeps at least one file in every group, so cleanup stays effortless and safe. 4. Disk Space Analysis See where your disk space is going at a glance. Switch between a treemap and a sunburst chart , and choose how many levels to display to explore space usage and folder structure. Browse folders alongside the file list to quickly find the largest folders and files and decide what to clean up. Privacy & Security 5. Privacy Cleanup Keep browsing history, searches, cookies, recent items, and clipboard data from lingering on your computer. Clear traces left by browsers, applications, and the system to reduce exposure of your activity and make everyday privacy easier to manage. System Tools 6. Application Uninstall and Cleanup Uninstall applications and clear related caches, settings, and leftovers so removing an application actually gives you the space back. Potential personal files are handled cautiously to reduce the risk of accidental deletion. 7. Startup Item Management Reduce unnecessary startup delays and background resource use, so your computer starts faster and feels lighter. Turn items back on at any time when you need them again. 8. System Optimization Reduce unnecessary settings that slow down your system or get in the way. Balance performance, privacy, and personal preferences so your computer feels faster and easier to use. 9. System Maintenance Fix common problems like missing search results, incorrect icons, no sound, or network connection failures—without hunting down fixes or typing complex commands. Get your computer back to normal sooner. Activity 10. Operation History Keep a clear record of every cleanup and system change. See how much space you recovered, what completed successfully, and whether anything still needs your attention. Resource Usage and Memory Management Available since version 1.1.1 Check CPU and memory usage, network speeds, and disk activity at a glance. See which apps use the most memory and free up memory with a click when resources are running low. Keep these details in your menu bar, taskbar, or system tray—no need to open the main window. AI Explanations Available since version 1.1.0 Unsure what an item does or what might happen if you change it? AI explanations use the item's description and current scan results to explain its purpose and what to consider before taking action. Spend less time looking things up and make more informed choices. Get explanations directly from items in Deep Cleanup (built-in rules), Privacy Cleanup, Startup Item Management, System Optimization, and System Maintenance. Official releases include free explanations each day, with the option to connect your own AI service. AI offers guidance; you decide which actions to take. Safety and Rules Important MangoDisk puts data safety ahead of reclaiming more space. Cleanup rules and system optimizations only ship after their safety boundaries are clearly defined and they pass validation on real systems. MangoDisk scans in read-only mode by default. Before cleanup, deletion, uninstall, or system setting changes begin, you can review and confirm exactly what will happen. Results are saved to Operation History. System Optimization only uses built-in, validated settings. It never accepts arbitrary registry paths, terminal commands, or scripts. MangoDisk reads each setting again after changing it and calls out high-impact items and changes that require administrator access or a restart. MangoDisk maintains its own cleanup rules. Third-party projects may provide research leads, but a candidate rule is only accepted after reliable sources, safe boundaries, and real-system behavior have been verified. Anything without a clear safety boundary is excluded. The complete rule library and revision history are open for inspection: view the MangoDisk cleanup rule library . Screenshots Deep Cleanup Find cleanable content across the system, applications, developer tools, and projects to reclaim more space Large File Cleanup Find the files taking up the most space without digging through folders Duplicate File Cleanup Safely remove exact duplicates while keeping at least one copy Disk Space Analysis See where your storage is going and quickly find the largest files and folders Startup Item Management Reduce unnecessary startup programs for faster sign-in and less background activity Application Uninstall and Cleanup Uninstall applications and remove related leftovers to reclaim more space System Optimization Optimize performance, privacy, and everyday usability in one click System Maintenance Fix common system issues quickly and get your computer back to normal Privacy Cleanup Leave fewer activity traces behind and keep everyday use more private Before You Begin Caution Cleanup, permanent deletion, and uninstall operations may not be reversible. Review the selected content and keep reliable backups of important data. Before running system maintenance or changing a startup item or system setting, make sure you understand its purpose and impact. Some system optimizations can affect security, privacy, battery life, or update behavior. Desktop App Download MangoDisk from the official download page or GitHub Releases , then follow the instructions for your operating system below. macOS Requirements: macOS Monterey 12.5 or later. Install with Homebrew: brew install --cask harry0703/tap/mangodisk Manual installation: Download the DMG from the official download page , open it, and drag MangoDisk into the Applications folder. Windows Requirements: 64-bit Windows 10 or later. Install with PowerShell: irm https: // get.mangodisk.app | iex Install with WinGet (official source): winget install -- id MangoDisk.MangoDisk -- exact -- source winget Manual installation: Download the Windows installer from the official download page and follow the installation prompts. Linux Recommended: Ubuntu 22.04 LTS or later, on x64 or ARM64. Available as .deb packages and AppImages.

others.title: Methodology for the application of generative artificial intelligence tools in higher design education
others.abstract: The rapid development of Generative Artificial Intelligence (GAI) technologies across both theoretical and practical domains is fundamentally transforming the epistemological and pedagogical foundations of higher design education. This study provides a comprehensive analysis of the methodological integration of generative AI tools, including ChatGPT, Claude, Midjourney, and DALL·E, in fostering creative thinking, critical analysis, and practical skills among design students in higher education institutions. The research examines the transition of studio pedagogy from traditional forms toward hybrid and dialogical models, the reinterpretation of Donald Schön’s concept of reflection-in-action within algorithmic environments, and the evolving role of the educator in AI-assisted learning processes. Methodologically, the study is grounded in a modified Technological Pedagogical Content Knowledge (TPACK) framework and a four-component Information and Communication Competence (ICC) model. The findings indicate that the systematic and purposeful implementation of GAI tools can increase students’ visual design production and productivity by approximately 14%; however, it may also lead to reduced diversity of ideas and an overreliance on algorithms for cognitive functions. To mitigate these risks, the study proposes the concepts of epistemic vigilance and process-oriented hybrid assessment mechanisms as essential components of contemporary design education.

others.title: Data drift monitoring in the maintenance of cascade software for detecting falsified digital information
others.abstract: The article considers the maintenance stage of cascade software for detecting falsified digital information, in which inexpensive classifiers resolve most messages and pass uncertain ones to a large language model. After deployment, the distribution of messages changes because of new narratives, new text generators and deliberate adaptation of adversaries, while true labels arrive with a delay or not at all. A system of seven monitoring signals is proposed, each linked to a component of the cascade and to the type of drift it reveals, and only one of them requires true labels. It is shown that in a cascade a covariate shift manifests primarily as growth of the escalation share, so that quality may remain stable while processing cost increases. To detect confident errors of the first tier that leave the escalation share unchanged, shadow escalation of a small random sample of first-tier decisions is proposed. An alarm rule based on non-overlapping confidence intervals and a graded response policy, from threshold recalibration to retraining and rollback, are described.

others.title: Trustworthy Phishing URL Detection Using Machine Learning: Performance Analysis and Future Directions
others.abstract: Over the years, Uniform Resource Locator (URL) Phishing has been a threat to online security because their scams exploit trust in a misleading URL to trick unsuspecting users into disclosing their username or passwords and other personal information. Not only that, but it is also crucial to identify these malicious URLs and ensure online platforms and users are protected. The ISCXURL2016 data was utilized for the purpose of analyzing the performance of different Machine Learning (ML) models in differentiating phishing and legitimate URLs in this paper. A wide range of classifiers were explored including the classic classifiers as well as more advanced ensemble classifiers. The results of the experiments indicate that ensemble-based boosting models can be more beneficial for URL phishing detection. HistGradientBoost achieved the highest accuracy of 98.47%, followed closely by LightGBM and XGBoost that both outperformed the accuracy of 98%. The other classifiers, RandomForest and ExtraTrees, also performed well with accuracy above 97% and traditional classifiers such as Quadratic Discriminant Analysis (QDA) showed the poorest performance with an accuracy of 67.75%. The results show that the boosting-based ensembles provide a suitable negation of the complex and non-linear structure of phishing URLs. Along with empirical evaluation, it offers a Properties & Positioning viewpoint as well as the importance of the ML-based phishing detection in the broader context of cybersecurity issues. Moreover, it discusses the future directions, with Federated Learning (FL) in the context of decentralized and privacy-preserving collaboration and Large Language Models (LLM) in the context of semantic reasoning and flexibility. These insights together will provide the building blocks for more intelligent, adaptive and trustworthy phishing organizations.

others.title: Cross-media affective differences in online reviews: aspect-level evidence and a dual-pathway mechanism
others.abstract:
This study investigates the micro-level structural differences in online review affect between social media and e-commerce platforms, exploring the underlying psychological mechanisms that drive consumers to selectively express polarised reviews across these media.
 
 
 
 Utilising large language model-driven aspect-based sentiment analysis, this study quantifies an initial dataset of 65,493 smartphone online reviews from TikTok, Bilibili, Jingdong and Suning to identify aspect-level affective differences. To explain the observed differences, Study 2 draws on uses and gratifications theory and conducts a 2 × 2 between-subjects experiment, using wireless headphones as the focal product and TikTok and Taobao as the platforms, to examine how media environments moderate the translation of consumption experiences into review intentions.
 
 
 
 Affective differences extend to specific cognitive attributes, with social media platforms exhibiting a significantly more negative and heterogeneous affective landscape, whereas e-commerce platforms demonstrate overwhelming positivity. These differences are driven by a dual-pathway mechanism. Social media platforms primarily activate self-enhancement motivation, which facilitates the translation of negative experiences into negative reviews while weakening the translation of positive experiences into positive reviews. Conversely, e-commerce platforms primarily activate economic motivation, which facilitates the translation of positive experiences into positive reviews while reducing the likelihood of negative experiences translating into negative reviews.
 
 
 
 This study extends the investigation of review affect from within-medium comparisons to cross-media analysis. By shifting from macro-level indicators to micro-level attribute evidence, this study reveals a more comprehensive picture of cross-media affective bias. By extending the application of uses and gratifications theory from content consumption to content production, it offers a novel mechanistic explanation for this phenomenon.

others.title: Can It Actually Work? Synthesizing Functional CAD Mechanisms
others.abstract: While LLM agents can generate visually plausible CAD assemblies, these designs often fail to fulfill their intended physical functions. We study functional CAD design, a setting where agents interpret underspecified requests to construct and iteratively revise mechanisms that satisfy functional requirements in physical simulation. Verifying these requirements is nontrivial: different candidate mechanisms may realize the same function through entirely different components, controls, and operating sequences. To bridge this gap, we propose FunCAD-Harness, a framework that translates abstract requirements into candidate-specific physical tests and uses simulation feedback to guide design revisions. To systematically evaluate this capability, we introduce FunCADBench, a benchmark spanning 46 mechanism families with interdependent and multi-step operations. Experiments across frontier LLM agents show that FunCAD-Harness exposes subtle mechanical failures invisible to visual inspection, substantially improving functional success rates over standard simulation-augmented baselines. Ultimately, our work marks a step toward CAD agents capable of translating human intent into working mechanisms.

others.title: Reinforcement Learning with Visually Attributable On-Policy Self-Distillation
others.abstract: Multimodal reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) provides reliable task-level supervision, yet offers limited guidance for localizing errors in visual reasoning. On-policy self-distillation (OPSD) complements this supervision with dense token-level corrections from a privileged teacher equipped with an evidence-centered visual view. However, the resulting corrections may conflate visual evidence with non-visual shifts induced by linguistic priors, response style, or the privileged view itself. We formalize this phenomenon as privileged-correction contamination: a token-level correction is contaminated when its update direction cannot be consistently attributed to the privileged visual evidence. Directly distilling contaminated corrections may therefore reinforce erroneous token-level updates. To address this issue, we propose reinforcement learning with visually attributable on-policy self-distillation, an evidence-consistent paradigm that augments task-level RLVR supervision with privileged token-level corrections grounded in visual evidence. We instantiate this paradigm with Visual-Attribution Gating (VAG), which uses the verifier-derived advantage as the optimization anchor and validates each privileged correction against the contrast between evidence-present and evidence-degraded teacher views. By admitting only corrections directionally supported by this visual contrast, VAG preserves visually grounded guidance while suppressing inconsistent residuals. Experiments across six visual reasoning benchmarks show that VAG consistently outperforms GRPO and OPSD methods, establishing new state-of-the-art average performance.

others.title: VideoMaMa++: Temporally Consistent Video Matting via Preserve-and-Refine Token
others.abstract: Diffusion-based video matting has recently emerged as a leading approach, leveraging video diffusion priors from internet-scale pretraining to achieve strong zero-shot generalization from limited synthetic data. However, the heavy compute of these diffusion backbones limits inference to a short chunk of just 6 to 24 frames, so even ordinary videos span multiple chunks. Because each chunk is matted independently from coarse mask guidance, existing methods fail to maintain consistency across chunk boundaries, producing flickering edges and discontinuous transparency. We address this with a mask-guided diffusion-matting framework built on two ideas. The RGB and mask conditioning are represented as separate token streams that interact through full spatio-temporal self-attention, letting the model adaptively combine fine RGB texture with coarse mask layout rather than committing to a fixed channel-wise fusion. On top of this, we propose a novel pair of learnable embeddings, the preserve token and the refine token, that act as a per-frame conditioning interface and enable a sliding-window inference scheme in which already-generated mattes are propagated across chunk boundaries for local temporal consistency, complemented by a globally shared reference anchor at every chunk to prevent error accumulation in long sequences without any additional training. Across standard video matting benchmarks and in-the-wild long footage, our framework outperforms prior diffusion-based methods in both fine-detail accuracy and temporal consistency, and uniquely maintains consistency across chunk boundaries on long videos.

others.title: Ropedia W0: Scaling Loco-Manipulation World Models across Embodiments with Human Experience
others.abstract: World models enable embodied agents to anticipate action consequences, yet jointly modeling locomotion and manipulation across diverse embodiments remains challenging due to heterogeneous action spaces and limited multimodal supervision. We present Ropedia W0, the first egocentric loco-manipulation world foundation model spanning humans and robots with diverse embodiments. We curate Xp-Data, comprising 10k hours of egocentric human data and 3k hours of robot data with unified multimodal annotations and systematic quality control. A unified kinematic representation encodes locomotion through camera poses and manipulation through projected skeletons, with robot skeletons combining embodiment-specific forward kinematics with extensive manual keypoint annotation and correction. We also introduce Xp-Teleop, a long-horizon loco-manipulation benchmark based on high-quality dexterous humanoid teleoperation data. Evaluations demonstrate state-of-the-art performance across five cross-embodiment benchmarks (DreamDojo, $Ψ_0$, $ω$-HOME, Xp-Teleop, and AgiBot) and on held-out human egocentric video, from zero-shot inference to few-shot and full-data post-training. Scaling human pre-training data improves performance on both human and robot evaluations. After distillation, our model supports real-time, minute-long rollouts, enabling live VR interaction. Applications in policy evaluation, model-based planning, and world-action modeling further demonstrate the model's utility for embodied decision-making.

others.title: CoopUQ: Robust Multi-Robot Social Navigation via Uncertainty-Aware Cooperative Forecasting
others.abstract: Reinforcement learning enables mobile robots to make fast and scalable navigation decisions in constrained human-shared environments. However, directly extending single-robot approaches to multi-robot settings often fails to ensure safety and efficiency, especially under occlusions and out-of-distribution (OOD) scenarios, where individual robots may overlook potential risks or make inaccurate predictions. Leveraging cooperation effectively for both prediction and navigation remains a major challenge. We propose CoopUQ, a multi-robot social navigation framework that bridges uncertainty-aware cooperative occupancy forecasting and robust decision making. CoopUQ predicts future occupancy grid maps through cross-robot spatiotemporal feature fusion and further leverages forecasts and their uncertainty to guide policy via constrained multi-agent reinforcement learning, where the cost penalizes navigation through regions predicted to be occupied or highly uncertain. This design enables the policy to adapt its risk sensitivity under distribution shifts. Experimental results across multiple Unity3D-based simulation environments with both in-distribution and OOD settings, including diverse layouts, pedestrian densities, and rushing behavior, demonstrate improved prediction performance and safety over representative baselines. Real-robot experiments further demonstrate its robustness across various scenes. Our code and videos are available at https://coopuq.github.io/.

others.title: GenOlympiad: Benchmarking Frontier Image Models at Their Capability Boundaries
others.abstract: Text-to-image models have made tremendous progress and can produce high-quality images. However, a question which would be asked in any other discipline is where the frontier models fall short. We introduce GenOlympiad, a benchmark which provides the most challenging text prompts from nine capability axes for stress-testing frontier text-to-image models. The assessed capabilities include generating large quantities, performing deep reasoning, ensuring hard physical consistency, following complex rules and so on. The prompts are designed such that prompt alignment is visually verifiable (e.g., counting) instead of relying on subjectiveness (e.g., style). Based on this, we develop an automated evaluation framework which decomposes the prompt into easy and hard questions, and for most hard questions, draws help lines to ground evidence for accurate grading. We evaluate 20+ strong text-to-image models, including Nano Banana Pro, GPT-Image-2.5, Seedream-5.0 and so on. We report that even the best-performing T2I model (Nano Banana Pro) only achieves a strict score of 23.9 out of 100 and that coding models such as GPT-6 Astra have higher prompt alignment scores (but not as visually pleasing). We also derive insights in model evolution, alignment with Elo scores, and effectiveness of our grounding-based evaluation protocol. Code is available at https://github.com/GenOlympiad/GenOlympiad and the project page is at https://genolympiad.github.io/

others.title: WeAct: Dynamic Weight Switching as Agent Actions
others.abstract: Long-horizon agents must learn heterogeneous capabilities from interleaved trajectories. Updating shared parameters to learn new capabilities can degrade previously acquired ones, resulting in catastrophic forgetting. As a trajectory unfolds, different stages may require different capabilities, yet conventional joint training and static adapter merging maintain a fixed parameter configuration throughout execution. We introduce WeAct (Weight-level Internal Actions), which trains independent capability-specific LoRA adapters over a frozen backbone and adds adapter selection to the agent's action space. These internal actions use the model's native tool-calling interface for on-demand capability composition in a shared context. Across eight deep-research benchmarks, Qwen3-32B with WeAct improves average accuracy by 6.2% relative to full fine-tuning counterparts despite using less compute, and by 27.5% relative to the strongest static LoRA-merging method. WeAct also supports modular continual adaptation, by adding a new code computation adapter to expand the agent's capabilities and updating the existing writing adapter to improve report quality. Both updates leave the backbone and other adapters unchanged, supporting modular continual adaptation in agents.

others.title: Train An Imaginative Agent
others.abstract: A seemingly reasonable push in Sokoban can make the puzzle unsolvable. To avoid such mistakes, an agent has to anticipate the consequences of its actions before execution, especially when feedback from the real environment is sparse or actions are irreversible. We introduce Agentic Imagination (Agima), a training framework that trains an agent to imagine before acting, i.e. to be imaginative. Agima trains a single omni model to propose actions, generate images of their outcomes, and then reason over these imagined futures to decide what to execute in the real environment. Rather than committing to a single plan, the agent can simulate a sequence of actions, explore alternatives, and compare possible futures. We first use supervised fine-tuning (SFT) to unify policy and world modeling within a single omni model. This enables the agent to predict future outcomes and perform basic forms of imagination, such as forward thinking and counterfactual branching. We then use agentic reinforcement learning (RL) to teach the agent to reason with its imagined futures and use them effectively for planning. Across four environments spanning Maze2D, Sokoban, Pacman, and PushT, Agima generalizes to harder settings unseen during training. Trained with SFT alone on two-box Sokoban, Agima solves 40% of four-box puzzles while seeing the real board only once every five moves, compared with an action-only planner that only solves 2%. After RL, new behaviors emerge in how Agima uses its imagination: it learns a new unified format that was unseen during the SFT stage, learns to conduct forward thinking only when necessary, and branches more frequently at critical decision points. An agent that can picture where its actions lead can learn when and where to look ahead, that is, to plan. Project page: https://agima.net/.

others.title: LatComm: Reusable Context Compression for Latent Communication between Large Language Models
others.abstract: Systems that combine several large language models (LLMs) often use one context for many questions. When the context is passed between models as text, the receiving model processes all of its tokens again for every question. Avoiding this cost requires a context representation that is compact, reusable across questions, and readable by a different LLM. Existing compression and latent communication methods each provide only some of these properties. We introduce LatComm, a Latent Communication interface that provides all three by separating encoding from reading: the context is encoded once without the question, and the receiver selects what to read for each question. A frozen context encoder LLM compresses the context into a fixed-size packet and sends it to a different frozen receiver LLM, which reads the packet through cross-attention, with gates computed from its prompt. On 12 multiple-choice question-answering datasets, LatComm improves average accuracy over single-vector baselines by up to 10.2 points. On QuALITY, it reduces the receiver's input by 57x and answers the questions of an article 3x faster.

others.title: Newton-Based Methods for Bilevel Optimization Beyond Lower-Level Strong Convexity
others.abstract: Bilevel optimization provides a framework for machine learning tasks such as hyperparameter optimization, data reweighting, and meta-learning. Existing Newton-based bilevel methods typically rely on the classical hypergradient formula, which is generally unavailable when lower-level solutions are nonunique and the lower-level Hessian is singular. We develop two Newton-based methods beyond lower-level strong convexity by exploiting curvature shared by the lower-level and multiplier updates. Newton-based GALET handles potentially singular lower-level curvature under a positive spectral-gap condition, exploiting its range structure to avoid the squared-Hessian multiplier system used in GALET. Newton-based BAMM uses a strongly convex aggregation model when the lower-level objective is convex and the upper-level objective is strongly convex in the lower-level variable. We establish convergence guarantees and improved complexity bounds relative to GALET and sl-BAMM under the corresponding assumptions. We further introduce GNBO, a generalized Newton-based framework that captures the shared-curvature structure of the proposed methods and several existing Newton and quasi-Newton bilevel methods. Experiments on synthetic problems, data hyper-cleaning, and GPT-2 data reweighting evaluate the proposed methods across different bilevel learning tasks.

others.title: SpecKCast: Spectral Kalman Forecasting for Diffusion Acceleration
others.abstract: Diffusion Transformers (DiTs) achieve high-fidelity image and video generation, but they suffer from substantial inference costs due to repeated transformer evaluations across many denoising steps. Feature caching reduces this cost by reusing features across denoising steps. Recent forecasting methods extend this idea by extrapolating features to skipped steps instead of reusing them. However, existing forecasting methods extrapolate the features they predict uniformly, even though the spatial-frequency components of these features change most at different stages of denoising. They also overlook that denoising progresses nonuniformly, so equal step intervals can correspond to very different amounts of change. These mismatches amplify forecast errors as more steps are skipped, limiting the achievable acceleration. We propose SpecKCast, a training-free method that forecasts the model output in the frequency domain. SpecKCast applies a 2D discrete cosine transform (DCT) to the output and tracks each coefficient with a lightweight Kalman filter along a band-specific time coordinate derived from the noise schedule. The filter tracks each coefficient's value and rate of change, and the transformer is evaluated only when the filter's forecast uncertainty exceeds a threshold. Experiments on FLUX.1-dev, Qwen-Image, Wan2.1-14B, and HunyuanVideo show that SpecKCast achieves a better trade-off between acceleration and fidelity than existing caching and forecasting methods, reaching up to 6x speedup with less than 0.05 GiB of additional memory.

others.title: Same Simulation, Different Evidence: Where Retrieved Tool Output Costs LLM Agents Accuracy
others.abstract: LLM agents that compute the right answer can still answer wrongly. Agent harnesses increasingly keep long tool outputs out of the context window, saving them to files that the agent searches or reads on demand. We ask where this costs accuracy with a real scientific tool: PHREEQC, a widely used geochemistry simulator from the USGS, whose reports reach 846.8k characters and whose determinism lets every printed value be traced. Agents use it to answer 158 execution-verified multiple-choice items. When agents read the simulator's report through a section index rather than in context, GPT-5.1 and GPT-5.2 lose 11.3 and 7.9 points of accuracy, while Claude Opus 4.6 and Claude Sonnet 4.6 show no detectable cost. Re-running all 11,007 logged simulator calls shows that both GPT models compute the keyed value about as often as before; what changes is the evidence they answer from. Under retrieval they often skip the report, answer from their own higher-precision output files, and misround to a neighboring option, a failure we call evidence substitution. With the simulation held fixed, retrieval still costs GPT-5.2 9.4 points. For GPT-5.4, more frequent correct simulations mask an evidence-use loss of about ten points, leaving a net change indistinguishable from zero. Naming the authoritative output raises accuracy by 6.3-7.9 points over plain retrieval for the three GPT models; for GPT-5.1 and GPT-5.2, inlining outputs that fit works as well, while asking for correct rounding does not. Context-management choices in agent harnesses should be judged by where accuracy is lost, not only by final accuracy.
